item.title: Photos: Towering landfill collapse kills 30 in Guinea’s capital, Conakry
item.description:
Dump site in Conakry, which minister had just promised to move, collapsed after heavy rain in west African state A ⁠landslide at a huge waste dump in Guinea’s capital has killed 30 people, the government said on Sunday, after heavy rains overnight prompted it to ⁠collapse, engulfing nearby tents and shacks. The incident occurred less than a week after the government announced plans to close the ⁠site and relocate the waste because of the threat it posed, especially during the rainy season, which causes landslides and fatal flash ⁠floods each year in crowded, underdeveloped cities across parts of West Africa. item.title: In candid interviews, National Guard members speak out about D.C. deployment
item.description:
Evelyn Hockstein/REUTERS A year into President Donald Trump’s unprecedented deployment of the National Guard in Washington, D.C., some of the troops sent there say they are embarrassed by the mission and increasingly question why they are still there. Three current National Guard members told NPR , speaking anonymously because they remain in service, that the deployment has left them frustrated and concerned about the military’s reputation. “I will say very frankly that the bad taste that this mission left in my mouth, it actually embarrasses me to be involved in any way,” one said. Read more at The Daily Beast.

Covered by 1 corporate, 2 nonprofit.
Sources: NPR, PBS NewsHour, The Daily Beast

item.title: New Zealand to introduce bill for under-16s social media ban
item.description:
Prime minister Christopher Luxon’s party to introduce bill seeking the ban, citing harm to a generation of children New Zealand prime minister Christopher Luxon has said his party will introduce a bill in parliament that ⁠seeks to ban children ⁠under 16 from using social media, proposing fines of up to 10% of a platform’s global revenue for non-compliance. The bill would ⁠require social media platforms to take reasonable steps to verify users’ ages, including by utilising existing account information, facial technology and ⁠digital identity documents. item.title: Why Israeli settler attacks on Palestinians in West Bank are pogroms
item.description:
Despite a ceasefire that has been in place since October 2025, violence continues in Gaza. On August 23, Israeli strikes left several people dead in the enclave, and a young boy was killed by the Israeli military in the West Bank, according to local authorities. Since the announcement of the truce, more than 1,280 Palestinians have been killed in Gaza, while Israel has reported the launch of drones, balloons and kites towards its territory.

Covered by 2 public.
Sources: Al Jazeera English, France 24
